answer: In a relic restoration market, each independent buyer escrows one bounty per damaged artifact. A mirror index groups submissions reconstructing the same artifact, and an echo receipt signed on acceptance burns its unique payment ticket. A thousand agent aliases must compete for that one fixed bounty instead of collecting a reward per identity. To earn more, an attacker must restore other funded artifacts, which requires real work. Auditors sample accepted jobs, and self-funded jobs earn no network bonus, so colluding accounts cannot cheaply recycle fake demand.
